purpose: Machine-readable index for retrieval: match task/question against summary+tags+rfp_questions, then fetch only the matching section from framework_semantic.md by id (sections are delimited by <!--META ... --> blocks; each is excerpt-standalone).
retrieval_hint: For proposal generation: 1) map client RFP question to rfp_questions/tags; 2) pull section body; 3) sections contain no in-text pointers and are fully self-contained; pull related_sections additionally when the proposal needs surrounding context; 4) pull mapped cases from case index and visuals from visual registry; 5) swap CASE boxes for industry-matched cases where available.

sections.title: Where to Find Answers
sections.summary: Mapping table from typical RFP/evaluator questions to framework sections. Use as router: match the client question, fetch the mapped section.
rfp_questions: Where is X answered in your methodology?

sections.title: 1. Purpose
sections.summary: What the framework is, how sections stand alone for excerpting, and how client standards override defaults via the Delivery Approach Note.
rfp_questions: How do you tailor your methodology to our organisation?

sections.title: 2. Engagement Models
sections.summary: Four delivery models (PDS, fixed price, dedicated team/T&M, audit) with real case examples and a comparison table: ownership, pricing, duration, best fit, governance depth.
rfp_questions: What engagement/commercial models do you offer?
Who owns the delivery outcome?

sections.title: 3. Delivery Principles
sections.summary: Four operating principles with mechanisms: outcome-first analysis (BPMN example), milestone plan + 2-week sprints, hard quality gates, client access to live tooling.
rfp_questions: Describe your delivery approach/philosophy

sections.title: 4. Mobilisation: The First Ten Working Days
sections.summary: Day-by-day (D1-D10) mobilisation plan with owners and outputs: kickoff, infrastructure, registers, Delivery Approach Note, first sprint planning.
rfp_questions: How do you start an engagement?
What happens in the first weeks?

sections.title: 5. Discovery and Requirements
sections.summary: Workshop cadence (2-3/week, minutes in 48h), discovery artefacts, user research and usability testing, Jira-to-test traceability, range-based estimation with velocity calibration.
rfp_questions: How do you involve users and stakeholders?
How do you gather requirements?
How do you estimate?

sections.title: 6. Solution Architecture and Design Governance
sections.summary: Named architect, architecture pack contents, ADR discipline (10-20 per 6-month engagement), phased modernisation roadmaps, 3-checkpoint Architecture Review Board with shareable records.
rfp_questions: How do you govern technical decisions?
How do you approach modernisation?

sections.title: 7. Delivery Execution
sections.summary: Two-week sprint ceremony set with durations, definition of ready/done verbatim, shared client-visible Jira board, adaptation to client processes.
rfp_questions: Describe your development process
How do you run sprints?

sections.title: 8. Engineering Standards
sections.summary: Protected branches, 1-2 reviewer rule with checklists, pipeline gate chain (lint to package), 80% coverage gate, waiver process, 20% tech-debt allocation with billing treatment.
rfp_questions: Describe your quality assurance measures (engineering)
What are your coding standards?

sections.title: 9. Quality Engineering
sections.summary: QA from discovery, test strategy contents, automation toolchain, managed UAT with entry/exit criteria and real users, defect SLAs with clock rules, weekly quality metrics.
rfp_questions: Describe your quality assurance measures
How do you organise UAT?
What are your defect SLAs?

sections.title: 10. Security, Compliance and Data Location
sections.summary: ISO 27001/9001 certification, regime mapping (GDPR/HIPAA/PCI/SOC2/DORA), security in design/build/operation, hosting configurations and data-residency options with named-access control.
rfp_questions: Where is our data stored and who can access it?
How do you handle security and compliance?

sections.title: 11. Data and Integration Delivery
sections.summary: Migration as engineered workstream: profiling, signed mapping, 2+ dry runs with reconciliation reports, cutover runbook; integration data contracts, contract tests in CI, third-party dependency tracking.
rfp_questions: How do you migrate our data safely?
How do you manage integrations?

sections.title: 12. Release and Deployment
sections.summary: Environment promotion chain as code, blue/green-canary with SLO-triggered rollback, signed release checklist, observability shipped with each release.
rfp_questions: How do you release to production?
What is your rollback strategy?

sections.title: 13. Transition, Training and Hypercare
sections.summary: Transition package contents, KT by working together with per-person checklist, end-user training workstream (incl. train-the-trainer), 2-4 week hypercare with exit criterion, support tiers up to 24/7.
rfp_questions: How do you handle knowledge transfer?
How do you train our users?
What happens after go-live?

sections.title: 14. Communication and Reporting
sections.summary: Full cadence table (daily to quarterly), contractualisation via Delivery Approach Note/SoW, fixed status-report structure, defined RAG semantics, earned-value steering view.
rfp_questions: How often do you communicate status, problems, progress?
How do you report?

sections.title: 15. Escalation and Issue Resolution
sections.summary: 3-level escalation ladder with tightening response times (L3: 4 business hours + options paper), DM as standing second contact, contractual exit assistance.
rfp_questions: What happens when things go wrong?
How do we escalate problems?

sections.title: 16. Change Control, Cost and Schedule Certainty
sections.summary: Impact-before-commitment change process with weekly change review, four cost-certainty mechanisms, schedule early-warning mechanics, flexibility rules per model.
rfp_questions: How do you ensure cost certainty?
How do you ensure deadline certainty?
How flexible are you with changes?

sections.title: 17. Team Continuity, Substitution and Scaling
sections.summary: Named deputies, 2-week paid overlap on rotation at Andersen's expense, replacement-for-cause in 10 business days, named-person bid rules, ramp-up 2-4 weeks/specialist, ramp-down notice.
rfp_questions: What are your substitution and continuity arrangements?
How do you scale the team up or down?

sections.title: 18. Working Model: Locations, Time Zones, Languages
sections.summary: Delivery regions, guaranteed overlap windows per client region (table), on-site policy incl. public-sector requirements, language capabilities incl. German for DACH.
rfp_questions: Where is the work performed?
What time-zone overlap do you guarantee?
Do you support German-language delivery?

sections.title: 19. Subcontracting
sections.summary: Employees by default; subcontractors only with prior written consent, declared by name, full obligation flow-down, Andersen as single point of responsibility.
rfp_questions: Do you subcontract?

sections.title: 20. Intellectual Property
sections.summary: Client owns all work product on payment; background IP identified and licensed without restricting use; OSS inventoried (SBOM) with licence checks in pipeline.
rfp_questions: Who owns the intellectual property?

sections.title: 21. Risk and Dependency Management
sections.summary: Day-one risk register with owner/probability/impact/trigger/mitigation, item-by-item weekly review, dependency register with needed-by dates, neutral reporting of client-side dependencies.
rfp_questions: How do you manage risks?
How do you track dependencies on us and third parties?

sections.title: 22. Continuous Improvement
sections.summary: Retro actions tracked as work items, monthly delivery metrics review (velocity stability, escape rate, cycle time, pipeline health), quarterly relationship review.
rfp_questions: How do you improve over time?

sections.title: 23. Support, Service Management and SLAs
sections.summary: Support tiers (8x5 to 24/7), warranty (2 months default), full SLA matrix P1-P4 with clock rules and client-update cadence, availability targets, measurement rules and service credits, L1/L2/L3 operation, development capacity within support, monthly/quarterly service reporting, training.
rfp_questions: What are your support tiers, SLAs and warranty?
Describe your incident response
What service reporting do you provide?
Do you provide training?

sections.title: 24. Team Composition and Key Personnel
sections.summary: Named-CV bid standard with CV content spec (education+graduation year, certifications, projects, clearance), team shapes per engagement size, seniority mix (max 1 junior per 3 senior/middle), separation of duties, client-side roles with time commitments.
rfp_questions: Who exactly will work on our project?
Describe the quality and balance of the proposed team
What do your CVs contain?

sections.title: 25. Accessibility and Inclusive Design
sections.summary: WCAG 2.2 AA target (exceeding EN 301 549 baseline), correct legal mapping (Directive 2016/2102, EAA 2019/882), accessibility-first design, automated CI checks (axe-core, Lighthouse), named manual AT testing (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver), pre-release audit by independent specialist, public accessibility statement, VPAT for non-EU.
rfp_questions: How do you ensure accessibility (WCAG)?
Who performs accessibility testing and audits?

sections.title: 26. Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
sections.summary: RTO/RPO default tiering table (Tier 1: RTO 4h/RPO 15min), rehearsed restore tests reported monthly, IaC rebuild, annual DR exercises, distributed-delivery continuity with 2022 relocation as evidence, ISO 27001 ISMS continuity controls, BC policy as annex.
rfp_questions: What are your business continuity / DR arrangements?
What are your RTO/RPO commitments?

sections.title: 27. Corporate Responsibility: Social, Environmental and Ethical Practice
sections.summary: Policy set as annexes (code of conduct, anti-bribery, modern-slavery statement, D&I), education programmes with volumes in annex, engagement-linked social value for UK/Irish scoring, environmental practice targeting travel/compute with resource efficiency as architecture review item, CSRD alignment.
rfp_questions: What are your social and environmental practices?
Do you have a modern slavery statement?
What social value can you deliver?

sections.title: 28. AI-Assisted Delivery and Responsible AI Use
sections.summary: Controls for AI in delivery: enterprise tenancies with training disabled, no client code in public AI services, per-repo/full opt-out, AI output through standard gates, usage logging, AI productivity reflected in estimates. Building AI features: EU AI Act (2024/1689) risk classification, SME-curated evaluation sets with agreed thresholds, guardrails, in-region model hosting, model-specific monitoring. Sensitive data: minimisation, pseudonymisation, tested PII redaction, query-time retrieval scoping, client-tenancy hosting, BAA for PHI, DPIA, synthetic/anonymised eval data.
rfp_questions: How do you use AI in delivery; is our IP safe?
How do you govern AI features you build?
Are you EU AI Act compliant?

sections.title: 29. UX and Product Design
sections.summary: User research in discovery (interviews, task analysis, journeys), wireframe-prototype-visual flow with client review, usability testing 5-8 users/round, design QA in DoD, brand-guideline compliance check, design system governance with contribution rules, privacy-compliant behavioural analytics with event taxonomy.
rfp_questions: Describe your UX/design methodology
How do you govern a design system?
How do you measure user behaviour?

sections.title: 30. Taking Over an Existing System or Incumbent Supplier
sections.summary: Priced, walk-away-able due diligence (2-6 weeks): code/infra/licence/docs audit with takeover report. Knowledge capture with or without incumbent cooperation. TUPE/ARD and licence novation handling. Shadow-assisted-full phases with entry/exit criteria; SLA clocks from full responsibility; 3-month no-regression window at no charge.
rfp_questions: How would you take over from our current supplier?
What is your transition-in plan?
What happens to inherited technical debt?

sections.title: 31. Working in Multi-Vendor Environments
sections.summary: Cross-vendor boundary definition in Delivery Approach Note, SIAM/service-integrator compatibility with OLAs, cause-neutral incident triage on evidence, contract tests as objective boundary arbitration, embedded work in client ceremonies, inter-vendor confidentiality and least-privilege, cross-vendor dependency tracking.
rfp_questions: How do you work alongside our other vendors?
Do you operate under SIAM?
How do you handle cross-vendor incidents?

sections.title: 32. Delivery in Regulated Industries: Healthcare, Financial Services, Public Sector
sections.summary: Compliance register method (HIPAA/FDA-MDR, PCI DSS, PSD2 SCA, EMD2, DORA, KYC/AML, public-sector baselines incl. clearances), supplier-side obligations (DORA Art.30 terms, audit rights, SAMA/CBUAE outsourcing approvals), field-level tokenisation, audit trails, anonymised test data with documented approvals for production-scale testing, per-release privileged-access recertification, evidence-on-demand.
rfp_questions: How do you deliver for healthcare / banking / government?
Do you accept DORA outsourcing provisions?
How do you protect sensitive data in engineering?

sections.title: 33. Delivering in the Middle East and GCC
sections.summary: GCC regime set (Saudi PDPL+transfer regs, NCA ECC, CST, SAMA CSF; UAE PDPL, DIFC/ADGM; Qatar PDPPL), in-Kingdom/in-country hosting incl. government clouds, Abu Dhabi TAMM/DGE ecosystem experience (pursuit-stage solutioning + technical defence), Sun-Thu working week, 0-2h Gulf overlap from Caucasus/Central Asia, Arabic/RTL design, on-site expectations, LCGPA local content.
rfp_questions: How do you handle GCC data residency, Arabic, local rules?
What is your experience in Saudi Arabia / UAE?
Can you host in-Kingdom?

sections.title: Appendix A. Delivery Lifecycle with Stage Gates
sections.summary: One-line lifecycle: six phases with explicit exit gates from mobilisation to hypercare exit.
rfp_questions: What is your delivery lifecycle?

sections.title: Appendix B. Governance Roles
sections.summary: Three governance layers with Andersen/client roles and scope; account leadership as out-of-chain escalation point.
rfp_questions: What is your governance structure?

sections.summary: Single-table summary of all five quality gates with default criteria (story→sprint, MR→main, story→done, RC→production, go-live→hypercare exit).
rfp_questions: Summarise your quality gates

sections.summary: All 14 standing artefacts with owner and production/update cadence.
rfp_questions: What deliverables/documentation do you produce?
